text: 是を見給て、大將軍左兵衞督知盛、「渡せや渡せ。」と下知せられければ、二萬八千餘騎、皆打入て渡しけり。馬や人に塞れて、さばかり早き宇治川の、水は上にぞ湛へたる。自ら外るゝ水には、何も不堪流れけり。雜人共は、馬の下手に取附々々渡りければ、膝より上をば濡さぬ者も多かりけり。如何したりけん伊賀伊勢兩國の官兵、馬筏押破られ水に溺れて六百餘騎ぞ流れける。萠黄、緋威、赤威、色々の鎧の浮ぬ沈ぬゆられけるは、神南備山の紅葉葉の、嶺の嵐に誘れて、龍田河の秋の暮、井塞に懸て、流もやらぬに異ならず。其中に緋威の鎧著たる武者が三人、網代に流れ懸て淘けるを、伊豆守見給ひて、

annotation.translation: Seeing this, the Great General Left Minister of the Imperial Guard, Tomomori, gave the order, 'Cross! Cross!' So twenty-eight thousand or more horsemen all charged in and crossed. The Uji River, so fast that it was choked by men and horses, stood still, its water swelling upward. The water that naturally flows could not withstand it. The commoners, attaching themselves to the horses' hindquarters and crossing one by one, were many who did not get wet above their knees. What became of the soldiers of Iga and Ise? text: 是等は三人ながら伊勢國の住人也。黒田後平四郎、日野十郎、乙部彌七と云ふ者なり。其中に日野十郎は、ふる者にて有ければ、弓の弭を岩の狹間にねぢ立て、掻上り、二人の者どもをも引上て、助たりけるとぞ聞えし。大勢みな渡して、平等院の門の内へ、入替／＼戰ひけり。此の紛に、宮をば南都へ先立て參せ、源三位入道の一類、殘て防矢射給ふ。

annotation.translation: These three were also residents of Ise Province: Kuroda Gohéi Shirō, Hino Jūrō, and Otobe Yashichi, who were called by these names. Among them, Hino Jūrō, being a skilled archer, twisted the nock of his bow into a crevice in a rock, climbed up, and pulled up the other two men, so it is said that he saved them. All the many crossed over and entered the gate of Byōdō-in, exchanging places and fighting. Amidst this confusion, they were told to send the Prince ahead to the Southern Capital, while the retinue of Gen Sanmi Nyūdō stayed behind to shoot arrows in defense.

text:
三位入道七十に餘て軍して、弓手の膝口を射させ、痛手なれば、心靜かに自害せんとて、平等院の門の内へ引退いて、敵おそひかゝりければ、次男源大夫判官兼綱、紺地の錦の直垂に、唐綾威の鎧著て、白葦毛なる馬に乘り、父を延さんと、返合せ／＼防戰ふ。上總太郎判官が射ける矢に兼綱内甲を射させて疼む處に、上總守が童、次郎丸と云ふしたゝか者押竝て引組でどうと落つ。源大夫判官は、内甲も痛手なれども、聞る大力なりければ、童を取て押て頸を掻き、立上らんとする處に、平家の兵共、十四五騎ひし／＼と落重て、兼綱を討てけり。伊豆守仲綱も、痛手あまた負ひ平等院の釣殿にて自害す。其頸をば下河邊藤三郎清親取て、大床の下へぞ投入ける。六條藏人仲家、其子藏人太郎仲光も、散々に戰ひ、分捕餘たして、遂に討死してけり。此仲家と申は、故帶刀先生義方が嫡子也。孤にて有しを、三位入道養子にして、不便にし給しが、日來の契を變ぜず、一所にて死にけるこそ無慚なれ。
三位入道は渡邊長七唱を召て、「我頸うて。」と宣へば、主の生頸討ん事の悲しさに、
涙をはらはらと流いて、「仕るとも覺え候はず。御自害候て、其後こそ給り候はめ。」
と申ければ、「誠にも。」とて西に向ひ、高聲に十念唱へ最後の詞ぞあはれなる。

annotation.translation: The Noble of the Third Rank, the tonsured priest, was over seventy years of age when he took up arms. He had an archer shoot at the crotch of his armor; since the wound was grievous, intending to commit seppuku with a calm heart, he withdrew inside the gate of Byodo-in. Because the enemy was drawing near, his second son, the Judge Gen-daiyu Kanezane, wearing a crimson brocade hitatare and a Tō-ayagane-yoroi armor, mounted a white ashitake horse, and striving to save his father, he turned to face the enemy and fought back and forth. When an arrow shot by the Sagami-no-tarō Judge pierced Kanezane's inner armor and caused him pain, Jiro-maru, a page of the Sagami-no-kami, who was a sturdy fellow, pushed forward, grappled with him, and fell down heavily. The Judge Gen-daiyu, though the wound to his inner armor was severe, being a man of great strength, took the page, pushed him down, and was about to scratch his neck when the Heike soldiers, numbering about fourteen or fifteen, descended upon him in a mass, and killed Kanezane. The Izu-no-kami Nakatsuna also received many wounds and committed seppuku at the Tsuri-den of Byodo-in. His neck was severed by the lower river-side person Fujisaburō Kiyochika and thrown down beneath the great platform. The Rokujo-no-daini Nakayoshi and his son, the Daini Tarō Nakamitsu, fought fiercely, took many spoils, and ultimately died in battle. This Nakayoshi was the legitimate son of the late Master Tachiba Yoshimasa. Having been an orphan, he was adopted by the Noble of the Third Rank, the tonsured priest, who treated him as if he were inconvenient, yet he did not change his loyalty and died alongside him; this is truly without shame. The Noble of the Third Rank summoned Watanabe Chōshichi and said, 'Cut off my neck.' Grieved by the sorrow of cutting off his lord's living neck, Chōshichi wept copiously and said, 'Even if I were to serve, I have no recollection of such a thing. You should commit seppuku yourself, and then I shall serve you.' Hearing this, he said, 'Truly so,' turned westward, loudly recited the Ten Nen, and the final words were most poignant.

text: 是を最後の詞にて、太刀のさきを腹に突立て、俯樣に貫てぞ失られける。其時に歌讀べうは無りしか共、若より強に好たる道なれば、最後の時も忘れ給はず。其頸をば唱取て泣々石に括合せ敵の中を紛れ出て、宇治川の深き所に沈てけり。

annotation.translation: With this as his final verse, he thrust the tip of his sword into his belly and fell forward, pierced through. At that time, although there was no one to read the poem, since he had loved it strongly from his youth, he did not forget it even at the end of his life. He took his neck in his mouth, tied it to the crying stone, and mingled among the enemies before emerging, and sank into the deep place of the Uji River.

text: 競瀧口をば平家の侍共、如何にもして、生捕にせんとうかゞひけれ共、競も先に心えて、散散に戰ひ、大事の手負ひ、腹掻切てぞ死にける。圓滿院大輔源覺、今は宮も遙に延させ給ひぬらんとや思ひけん。大太刀大長刀左右に持て、敵の中をうち破り、宇治川へ飛で入り、物具一つも捨ず、水の底を潜て、向の岸に渡り著き、高き所に登り、大音聲を揚て、「如何に平家の君達、是までは御大事かよう。」とて、三井寺へこそ歸けれ。

annotation.translation: The Heike warriors, though they sought with every means to capture Tategaki alive, Tategaki had anticipated this beforehand; he fought scatteredly, receiving a serious wound, cut open his belly, and died. Gen no Suke, the Abbot of Man'en-in, must have thought, 'Now His Imperial Majesty will surely be spared for a long time.' Holding the great sword and the great naginata in both hands, he broke through the midst of the enemy, leaped into the Uji River, leaving not a single piece of armor behind, dived to the bottom of the water, crossed to the opposite shore, climbed to a high place, raised his great voice, and said, 'How greatly have the Heike lords suffered up to this point!' Then he returned to Mii-dera.

text: 飛騨守景家は、古兵にて有ければ、此紛に、宮は南都へやさきたゝせ給ふらんとて軍をばせず、其勢五百餘騎、鞭鐙を合せて追懸奉る。案の如く、宮は三十騎許で落させ給けるを、光明山の鳥居の前にて、追附奉り、雨の降る樣に射參せければ、何が矢とは覺ねども、宮の左の御側腹に矢一筋立ければ、御馬より落させ給て、御頸取れさせ給ひけり。是を見て御伴に候ける鬼佐渡、荒土佐、荒大夫、理智城房の伊賀公、刑部俊秀、金光院の六天狗、何の爲に命をば惜むべきとて、をめき叫んで討死す。

annotation.translation: The Governor of Hida, Kageie, being an old soldier, fearing that the Prince would go to Nara, did not engage the enemy; instead, with his force of over five hundred cavalrymen, they joined spurs and whips in pursuit. As expected, the Prince was allowed to fall with about thirty riders; before the torii of Mount Kōmyō, they caught up with him and shot at him like rain. Though he did not realize what kind of arrows they were, one arrow pierced his left side, causing him to fall from his horse and have his neck cut off. Seeing this, his companions, Oni no Sado, Aradoza, Aradaifu, the Iga no Kō of Jichijōbō, Shōbu Toshimitsu, and Rokutengu of Kōkōin, thinking, "What is there to cherish life for?", screamed in anguish and died fighting.

text: 其中に宮の御乳母子、六條助大夫宗信敵は續く、馬は弱し、にゐ野の池へ飛でいり、浮草顏に取掩ひ、慄居たれば、敵は前を打過ぬ。暫し有て兵者共の四五百騎、さゞめいて打ち歸ける中に、淨衣著たる死人の、頸も無いを、蔀の下にかいていできたりけるを誰やらんとみ奉れば、宮にてぞましましける。我死ば此笛をば御棺に入よと仰ける小枝と聞えし御笛も、未御腰に差れたり。走出て取も附まゐらせばやと思へども、怖しければ其も叶はず。かたき皆歸て後、池より上り、ぬれたる物共絞著て、泣々京へ上たれば、憎まぬ者こそ無りけれ。

annotation.translation: Among them, the Emperor's wet nurse, Rokujo no Sukedai no Mune Nobu, was followed by the enemy; his horse was weak, so he leaped into Inui Pond, covered his face with floating grass, and trembled there, causing the enemy to pass him by. After a while, among the four or five hundred soldiers clamoring and returning, when they saw a corpse wearing a white robe, without a head, pulled out from beneath a lattice, wondering who it might be, they discovered it was the Emperor himself. He had ordered, "When I die, place this flute in my coffin." The small branch said to be the flute he spoke of was still not yet placed at his waist. Although they thought, "Let us rush out and take him," they were too afraid to do so. After all the enemies had returned, he climbed out of the pond, wrung out his wet clothes, and weeping, ascended to Kyoto. Indeed, there was no one who did not hate him.

text: 去程に南都の大衆ひた甲七千餘人、宮の御迎に參る。先陣は粉津に進み、後陣は未興福寺の南大門にゆらへたり。宮は早光明山の鳥居の前にて討れさせ給ぬと聞えしかば、大衆みな力及ばず涙を押へて留りぬ。今五十町許待附させ給はで、討れさせ給けん宮の御運の程こそうたてけれ。

annotation.translation: On the outward journey, the multitude of Nanto, numbering over seven thousand in full armor, came to welcome the Palace. The vanguard advanced to Konotsu, while the rear guard wavered at the South Great Gate of the newly built Kofuku-ji. When it was heard that the Palace had been slain before the torii of Hayakōmyō-san, the multitude, all powerless to help, held back their tears and remained. If only they had waited for about fifty cho, the Palace's fortune to be slain would have been most wretched.

text: 平家の人々は宮竝びに三位入道の一族、三井寺の衆徒、都合五百餘人が頸、太刀長刀のさきに貫き、高く指上げ、夕に及で六波羅へ歸入る。兵共勇のゝしる事夥し。怖しなども愚也。其中に源三位入道の頸は、長七唱が取て宇治川の深き所に沈てければ、それは見ざりけり。子供の頸はあそこ爰より皆尋出されたり。中に宮の御頸は、年來參り寄る人も無れば、見知り參せたる人もなし。先年典藥頭定成こそ、御療治の爲に召たりしかば、其ぞ見知り參せたるらんとて召れけれども、現所勞とて參らず。宮の常に召されける女房とて、六波羅へ尋ね出されたり。さしも淺からず、思食されて、御子を産參せ最愛ありしかば、爭か見損じ奉るべき。只一目見參せて、袖を顏に推當て、涙を流されけるにこそ、宮の御頸とも知てけれ。

annotation.translation: The people of the Heike, together with the three-level priestly family and the monks of Miidera Temple, totaling over five hundred, were pierced through the necks with the tips of long swords and daggers, held up high, and brought back to the Rokuhara district as evening approached. The soldiers displayed great courage; even words like 'fearful' are foolish. Among them, the head of the Genji three-level priest was taken down by seven men and sunk into the deep waters of the Uji River, so it could not be seen. The heads of the children were all searched for and found there and here. As for the Princess's head, since no one had come to visit in many years, there was no one who knew her. In previous years, the Chief Physician Sadanari was summoned for her treatment, and he was the one who might have known her; however, when he was summoned again, he did not come, claiming it was a burden at the current location. A lady-in-waiting who had always been summoned to the Princess's side was sent to the Rokuhara to search for her. Since she had been greatly cherished, having borne the Princess's beloved child, how could anyone have failed to recognize her? Only after seeing her face once and pressing a sleeve to her cheek, shedding tears, did they realize it was the Princess's head.

text: この宮は、腹々に御子の宮達あまた渡らせ給ひけり。八條女院に伊豫守盛教が娘、三位局とて候はれける女房の腹に、七歳の若宮、五歳の姫宮御座けり。入道相國、弟池中納言頼盛卿を以て、八條女院へ申されけるは、「高倉宮の御子の宮達のあまた渡らせ給候なる。姫宮の御事は申に及ばず、若宮をば、疾う／＼出し參させ給へ。」と申されたりければ、女院御返事に、「かゝる聞えの有し曉、御乳人などが、心少う具し奉て失にけるにや、全く此御所に渡せ給はず。」と仰ければ、頼盛卿力及ばで此由を入道相國に申されけり。「何條其御所ならでは、何くへか渡せ給ふべかんなる。其儀ならば、武士共參て、搜奉れ。」とぞ宣ける。此中納言は、女院の御乳母、宰相殿と申す女房に相具して、常は參り通れければ、日來は懷うこそ思召つるに、此宮の御事申しに參られたれば、今はあらぬ人の樣に疎しうぞ思召されける。若宮、女院に申させ給けるは、「是程の御大事に及び候上は終には遁れ候まじ。とう／＼出させ御座ませ。」と申させ給ければ、女院御涙をはら／＼と流させ給ひて、「人の七つ八つは、何事をも聞分ぬ程ぞかし。其に我故、大事の出來たる事を、片腹痛く思て、か樣に宣ふいとほしさよ。由無かりける人を、此六七年手馴して、かかる憂目を見よ。」とて、御涙せきあへさせ給はず。頼盛卿、宮出し參らさせ給ふべき由重ねて申されければ、女院力及ばせ給はで、終に宮を出しまゐらさせ給ふ。御母三位局、今を限の別なれば、さこそは御名殘惜うも思はれけめ。泣泣御衣著奉り、御髮掻撫で、出し參せ給ふも、唯夢とのみぞ思はれける。女院を始參せて、局の女房、女童に至るまで、涙を流し袖を絞らぬは無りけり。

annotation.translation: This palace had dispatched many of the Imperial children to various places. At the residence of the Imperial Lady of Hachijō, in the womb of a lady-in-waiting named Iyo-no-kami Morinori's daughter, who was known as the Lady of the Third Rank, there were an Imperial child of seven years and a Princess of five years. The Retired Imperial Prince, the Chancellor of State, sent the Imperial Councilor Yorisuke, his younger brother, to the Imperial Lady of Hachijō, saying, "Many of the children of Emperor Takakura have already been dispatched to other places. There is no need to speak of the Princess, but the Imperial child must be sent out at once." Since this was reported to her, the Imperial Lady replied, "In such a time of great disturbance, might it not be that the wet nurses and others have grown somewhat lax in their duties, and thus have not sent them to this place?" The Chancellor of State, finding his efforts in vain, reported this to the Retired Imperial Prince, the Chancellor of State. "Aside from this residence, to where else can they be sent? If this is the case, let the warriors go and search." Thus it was proclaimed. This Imperial Councilor, having often accompanied the Imperial Lady's wet nurse, the lady known as the Chamberlain's Lady, had grown very fond of the palace over the years. However, when this matter of the palace was brought to his attention, he now felt that it was someone else's affair and grew distant. The Imperial child, through the Imperial Lady, said, "Since this great matter has come to this point, we cannot ultimately escape. Please, let us be sent out without delay." Hearing this, the Imperial Lady shed tears profusely and said, "Children of seven or eight years do not yet understand anything. It is for this reason that, when such a grave incident occurs, I feel such deep sorrow and distress. After having raised this person, who had no fault, for six or seven years, now to see such a wretched sight." She could not hold back her tears. Since the Imperial Councilor repeatedly urged that the palace be sent out, the Imperial Lady, though unable to resist, finally allowed the palace to depart. The Imperial child's mother, the Lady of the Third Rank, now facing a parting as if it were her last, surely felt great sorrow. She dressed him, combed his hair, and sent him off, yet she could only think of it as a dream. From the Imperial Lady down to the ladies-in-waiting and even the young girls, all wept and wrung their sleeves.

text: 頼盛卿、宮請取參せ、御車に乘奉て、六波羅へ渡し奉る。前右大將宗盛卿此宮を見參せて、父の相國禪門の御前に坐て、「何と候やらん、此宮を見奉るが、餘に痛う思ひ參せ候。理を枉て此宮の御命をば、宗盛に賜候へ。」と申されければ、入道「さらばとう／＼出家をせさせ奉れ。」とぞ宣ける。宗盛卿、此由を八條女院に申されければ、女院「何の樣もあるべからず、唯疾々。」とて法師になし奉り、釋氏に定らせ給ひて、仁和寺の御室の御弟子になし參させ給ひけり。後には東寺の一の長者、安井宮僧正道尊と申しは、此宮の御事なり。

annotation.translation: Tadamori no kō, please take this palace. Ride in the carriage and convey it to Rokuhara. The former Right Great Captain, Mochimori no kō, seeing this palace, sat before his father, the Chancellor of State Zenmon, and said, 'What shall I do? Seeing this palace makes me exceedingly sorrowful. If I were to bend the law and grant this palace's life to Mochimori,' then the Cloistered said, 'Then let him be ordained immediately.' Mochimori no kō reported this to the Lady of the Eighth Street, and she said, 'There is no other way; quickly enough.' She had him become a monk, established him as a Buddhist priest, and made him a disciple in the Imperial Chamber of Ninna-ji Temple. Later, the foremost elder of the Eastern Temple, the Dignitary Monk Shōdō of the Yasui Palace, was the one who dealt with this palace's affairs.

text: 又奈良にも一所座しけり。御乳母讃岐守重秀が御出家せさせ奉り、具し參らせて、北國へ落下りたりしを、木曽義仲上洛の時主にし進せんとて、具し奉て都へ上り、御元服せさせ參らせたりしかば、木曽が宮とも申けり。又還俗の宮とも申けり。後には嵯峨の邊、野依に渡らせ給ひしかば、野依の宮とも申けり。

annotation.translation: Moreover, she also resided in a place in Nara. Her wet nurse, Saiki-no-Kami Shigehide, had her become a nun and had her go forth, and she had descended to the northern provinces; when Kiso Yoshinaka came to the capital, intending to have her as his principal wife and present her with gifts, she went up to the capital with her gifts, and had her come of age ceremony performed for her, and thus she was called the Kiso Palace. She was also called the Palace of Reverting to Lay Life. Later, she was transferred to the vicinity of Saga, to Noiri, and thus she was called the Noiri Palace.

text: 昔通乘といふ相人有り。宇治殿二條殿をば、君三代の關白、共に御年八十と申たりしも違はず。帥内大臣をば、流罪の相在すと申たりしも違はず。聖徳太子の、崇峻天皇を横死の相在ますと申させ給ひたりしが、馬子大臣に殺され給ひにき。さも然るべき人々は、必ず相人としもあらねども、かくこそ目出たかりしか。是は相少納言が不覺にはあらずや。中比兼明親王、具平親王と申しは、前中書王、後中書王とて、共に賢王聖主の王子にて渡せ給ひしかども、位にも即せ給はず。され共何かは謀反を起させ給ひし。又後三條院第三の皇子、資仁親王も御才學勝て御座ければ、白河院未東宮にておはしまいし時「御位の後は、此宮を位には即參らさせ給へ。」と、後三條院、御遺詔有しかども、白河院如何思召されけん、終に位にも即け參らさせ給はず、責ての御事には、資仁親王の御子に、源氏の姓を授け參らさせ給て、無位より一度に三位に叙して、軈て中將に成參らさせ給ひけり。一世の源氏、無位より三位する事嵯峨皇帝の御子、陽院の大納言定卿の外は是始とぞ承る。花園左大臣有仁公の御事なり。

annotation.translation: In ancient times, there was a man named Tsuusho. It was not untrue that His Excellencies Uji and Nijo, both the three generations of the Sessho and Kampaku, were said to be eighty years old. Nor was it untrue that the Captain, the Minister of the Interior, was said to be in exile. The Holy Prince Taishi declared that Emperor Sushun met a violent death, yet he was killed by Minister Kume. Such people, though not necessarily fortune-tellers, were indeed fortunate to be so. Was this not due to the fortune-teller Sho-na-gon's lack of insight? Prince Kanemi and Prince Tadahira, known respectively as former and latter Chusho-no-ko, were both wise princes and sons of sages, yet they did not ascend to the throne. Yet somehow, they were made to instigate a rebellion. Furthermore, the third son of Emperor Go-Sanjo, Prince Sanehito, was gifted in talent and learning; when Emperor Shirakawa, who had not yet been Crown Prince, was alive, he said, 'After my reign, let this prince ascend to the throne.' Although Emperor Go-Sanjo left a testament to this effect, how Emperor Shirakawa may have thought, in the end, he did not allow him to ascend to the throne. Instead, he bestowed the Minamoto surname upon Prince Sanehito's son, promoted him from a rankless status directly to the Third Rank, and later made him Middle Captain. I have heard that among the Minamoto of this generation, the only one to rise from rankless status to the Third Rank, aside from Emperor Saga's son, Prince Dajo-ken of the Great Palace, Sadanaga, was this beginning. This concerns Prince Arinobu, the Left Minister of Hanazono.

高倉宮の御謀反の間、調伏の法承はて修せられける高僧達に勸賞行はる。前右大將宗盛卿の子息侍從清宗三位して、三位侍從とぞ申ける。今年纔に十二歳。父の卿も、此齡では兵衞佐でこそおはせしか。忽に上達部に上り給ふ事、一の人の公達の外は、いまだ承り及ばず。源茂仁、頼政法師父子追討の賞とぞ除書には有ける。源茂仁とは、

ましき。

annotation.translation: During the time of Prince Takakura's rebellion, the great monks who had completed the rituals of subjugation were rewarded. The son of the former Right Great Captain, Suke-mori-no-kimi, was appointed to the position of Junior Third Rank and Attendant in the Palace; he was called the Junior Third Rank Attendant. This year, he was only twelve years old. His father, the Great Captain, had been a Hyoe-no-suke at that age. That he should suddenly rise to the rank of Upper Rank is something that, except for one person among the public officials, no one has yet heard of. Gen Shōnin and the priest Raihō, father and son, were listed in the official decree as recipients of the reward for the pursuit and elimination of Prince Shōnin. Gen Shōnin was none other than Prince Takakura. Even to strike down a son of the retired Emperor, the righteous Taihō Hōkō, is a matter of deep contempt for any commoner.

text: さてこそ三位はしたりけれ。軈て出家して、源三位入道とて、今年は七十五にぞ成れける。此人一期の高名と覺し事は、近衞院御在位の時、仁平の頃ほひ、主上夜々おびえたまぎらせ給ふ事有けり。有驗の高僧貴僧に仰て、大法秘法を修せられけれども、其驗なし。御惱は丑刻許で在けるに、東三條の森の方より、黒雲一村立來て、御殿の上に掩へば、必ずおびえさせ給ひけり。是に依て公卿僉議有り。去る寛治の比ほひ、堀河天皇御在位の時、しかの如く、主上夜な／＼おびえさせ給ふ事在けり。其時の將軍義家朝臣、南殿の大床に候はれけるが、御惱の刻限に及で、鳴絃する事三度の後、高聲に「前陸奧守、源義家」と名乘たりければ、人人皆身の毛堅て、御惱怠せ給ひけり。然れば即先例に任て、武士に仰て警固有べしとて、源平兩家の兵の中を選せられけるに、此頼政を選出れたりけるとぞ聞えし。此時は未兵庫頭とぞ申ける。頼政申けるは、「昔より朝家に武士を置るゝ事は、逆反の者を退け、違勅の輩を亡さんが爲なり。目にも見えぬ變化の物仕れと仰せ下さるゝ事、未承り及ばず。」と申ながら、勅定なれば召に應じて參内す。頼政は憑切たる郎等、遠江國の住人、井早太に、ほろのかざきりはいだる矢負せて、唯一人ぞ具したりける。我身は二重の狩衣に、山鳥の尾を以て作だる鋒矢二筋、滋籐の弓に取添て、南殿の大床に伺候す。頼政矢を二つ手挾ける事は、雅頼卿其時は未左少辨にて坐けるが、變化の者仕らんずる仁は、頼政ぞ候と選び申されたる間、一の矢に變化の物を射損ずる者ならば、二の矢には、雅頼の辨の、しや頸の骨を射んとなり。日來人の申に違はず、御惱の刻限に及で、東三條の森の方より、黒雲一村立來て、御殿の上にたなびいたり。頼政吃と見上たれば、雲の中に恠き物の姿あり。是を射損ずる者ならば、世に有るべしとは思はざりけり。さりながらも矢取て番ひ、南無八幡大菩薩と、心の中に祈念し、能引て、ひやうと射る。手答して、はたと中る。「得たりやをう」と、矢叫をこそしたりけれ。井早太つと寄り、落る處をとて押へて、續樣に九刀ぞ刺たりける。其時上下手々に火を燃いて、是を御覽じ見給ふに、頭は猿、躯は狸、尾は蛇、手足は虎の姿也。鳴く聲ぬえにぞ似たりける。怖しなども愚なり。主上御感の餘に、獅子王といふ御劔を下されけり。宇治左大臣殿是を賜り次で、頼政に賜んとて、御前のきざはしを半許下させ給へる處に、比は卯月十日餘の事なれば、雲井に郭公、二聲三聲音信てぞ通りける。其時左大臣殿

annotation.translation: Now indeed the Daisan was present. Soon after, he became a priest, known as Gen Daisan Nyudo, and this year he turned seventy-five. The notable matter concerning this person's life was that during the reign of the Konoe-in, around the time of the Ninpei era, His Majesty was frightened night after night. Although he consulted with eminent and noble monks to practice the great and secret dharma, there was no effect. His Majesty's affliction occurred around the hour of the ox. From the direction of the forest of Higashi-Sanjo, a black cloud rose like a village and covered the palace, and His Majesty was always frightened. Because of this, the nobles convened and discussed it. In the past, during the reign of Emperor Kōkō in the era of Kanji, just as before, His Majesty was frightened night after night. At that time, the Shogun, Yoshikage no Asomi, was waiting on the great floor of the Nan-den. When the time of the affliction arrived, after the three times of plucking the strings, he loudly proclaimed, 'Former Governor of Mutsu, Gen Yoshikage,' and everyone's hair stood on end, and the affliction ceased. Therefore, following the precedent, it was decided to assign samurai for protection, and from among the troops of the Gen and Hei families, this Yorimasa was selected, as we have heard. At that time, he was called Hyōgo no Kami. Yorimasa said, 'Since ancient times, placing samurai in the Imperial household is to repel rebels and eliminate those who disobey imperial edicts. Regarding matters of unseen transformations that are said to be done by His Majesty, I have never heard of such things.' Nevertheless, since it was an imperial decree, he responded to the summons and entered the palace. Yorimasa took the sword-drawing samurai, Ijida of Suruga Province, and had him carry the special arrows known as horo-gazaki. He alone prepared himself. His body was clad in a double-layered hunting robe, with two shafts of arrowheads made from mountain pheasant feathers, attached to a wisteria bow. He awaited service on the great floor of the Nan-den. Yorimasa held two arrows in his hands. At that time, the noble Akira was seated as the left junior counselor. Since it was decided that Yorimasa would deal with any transforming creature, if the first arrow failed to strike the transforming being, the second arrow would be aimed to pierce Akira's neck. As the people had predicted, when the time of the affliction arrived, from the direction of the forest of Higashi-Sanjo, a black cloud rose like a village and hovered over the palace. When Yorimasa looked up in surprise, there was a strange creature in the cloud. If one failed to strike it down, he thought, it would surely remain in the world. Nevertheless, he took an arrow, took his turn, and prayed in his heart, 'Namu Hachiman Daibosatsu,' drew the bow with great strength, and shot with a swift motion. The arrow responded and struck instantly. 'I have caught it!' he shouted, raising the arrow. Ijida rushed over, pinned it down where it fell, and pierced it with nine swords without pause. At that moment, the upper and lower attendants lit fires, and His Majesty viewed the scene. The head was that of a monkey, the body a tanuki, the tail a snake, and the limbs those of a tiger. Its cry resembled a human wail. Fear and the like were foolish. Overcome with emotion, His Majesty bestowed the sword named Shishō. The Left Minister of Uji received it and intended to give it to Yorimasa, ordering the lowering of half the steps before the throne. text: 去る應保の比ほひ、二條院御在位の御時、ぬえと云ふ化鳥、禁中に鳴て、屡宸襟を惱す事有き。先例を以て、頼政を召されけり。比は五月二十日餘のまだ宵の事なるに、ぬえ唯一聲音信て、二聲とも鳴ざりけり。目指とも知ぬ闇では有り、姿形も見えざれば、矢つぼを何とも定めがたし。頼政策に先大鏑を取て番ひ、ぬえの聲しつる内裏の上へぞ射上たる。ぬえ鏑の音に驚て虚空に暫ひゝめいたり。二の矢に小鏑取て番ひ、ひいふつと射切て、ぬえと鏑と竝べて前にぞ落したる。禁中さざめきあひ、御感斜ならず、御衣を被させ給けるに、其時は、大炊御門右大臣公能公是を賜りついで、頼政にかづけさせ給ふとて、「昔の養由は、雲の外の鴈を射き、今の頼政は、雨の中のぬえを射たり。」とぞ感ぜられける。

annotation.translation: In the time of the late Jōhō period, during the reign of Emperor Nijō, a transformation bird called nue cried out in the inner palace, causing frequent distress to the imperial person. In accordance with precedent, Yorimasa was summoned. At this time, on the evening of about the twentieth day of the fifth month, the nue, making only one sound, did not cry out with two voices. Though it was an utterly dark place where one could not even know the direction, and its form could not be seen, it was difficult to determine where to aim. Yorimasa took the large arrowhead of the policy first, nocked it, and shot it up toward the palace where the sound of the nue was. Startled by the sound of the arrowhead, the nue fluttered for a while in the void. Taking the small arrowhead for the second arrow, he nocked it, and with a single shot, cut it down, causing both the nue and the arrowhead to fall down together. The inner palace buzzed with commotion; the Emperor was not displeased, and he had his robes put on for him. At that time, he bestowed upon Tōfukumon In no Dainagon Kōno Kō, and had it given to Yorimasa, saying, 'In ancient times, Yōyū shot a goose beyond the clouds; now, Yorimasa has shot the nue in the rain.'

text: と仕り、御衣を肩に懸て退出す。其後伊豆國賜はり、子息仲綱受領になし、我身三位して、丹波の五箇庄、若狹のとう宮河を知行して、さて坐べかりし人の、由なき謀反起て、宮をも失參せ我身も子孫も亡ぬるこそうたてけれ。

annotation.translation: Thus he said, and, having draped the robe over his shoulders, he withdrew. Later, he was granted the province of Izu, his son Nakatsuna was appointed as a governor, he himself became a noble of the third rank, and he exercised control over the five manors of Tango and the Toumiya River in Wakasa. Yet, the person who had once been seated here, having risen up in a baseless rebellion, lost even the palace, and both he himself and his descendants perished; this is truly tragic.

日ごろは山門の大衆こそ、亂りがはしき訴仕るに、今度は穩便を存じて音もせず。南都三井寺或は宮請取奉り、或は宮の御迎に參る。是以て朝敵也。されば三井寺をも南都をも攻らるべしとて、同五月二十七日、大將軍には入道の四男頭中將重衡、副將軍には薩摩守忠度、都合其勢一萬餘騎で園城寺へ發向す。寺にも堀ほり、かい楯掻き、
逆茂木引て待かけたり。卯刻に矢合して、一日戰ひ暮す。防ぐ所の大衆以下法師原三
百餘人まで討れにけり。夜軍に成て、暗さはくらし、官軍寺中に攻入て、火を放つ。燒る所、本覺院、成喜院、眞如院、花園院、普賢堂、大寶院、清瀧院、教待和尚本坊、竝に本尊等、八間四面の大講堂、鐘樓、經藏、灌頂堂、護法善神の社壇、新熊野の御寶殿、惣じて堂舎塔廟六百三十七宇、大津の在家一千八百五十三宇、智證の渡し給へる一切經七千餘卷、佛像二千餘體、忽に煙と成こそ悲しけれ。諸天五妙の樂も、此時長く盡き、龍神三熱の苦も彌盛なるらんとぞ見えし。

annotation.translation: As usual, the multitude at the Mountain Gate were the ones making loud complaints, but this time, considering it prudent, they made no sound. Some went to the Southern Capital's Miidera to petition the Imperial Court, others went to welcome the Emperor's reception. For this reason, they are enemies of the court. Therefore, it was decided that both Miidera and the Southern Capital should be attacked, and on the 27th of the same month, the Great General was the monk's fourth son, the Captain-General Jujo Shokei, and the Vice-General was the Governor of Satsuma, Tadazane, with a total force of over ten thousand cavalry advancing toward Ojoji Temple. The temple had dug moats, set up palisades, and prepared hidden stakes to wait. At the hour of the Rabbit, they engaged in a rain of arrows and fought until nightfall. The defending multitude, down to the three hundred and more monks at the Monks' Plain, were all slain. At night, it became an army; the darkness was dark, and the Imperial forces charged into the temple, setting fire. The places burned were Honkaku-in, Nishiki-in, Shinko-in, Hanazono-in, Fugen-do, Taiho-in, Seiryu-in, the head priest of Kyotai's main hall, and also the principal images; the great lecture hall, eight ken on each side, the bell tower, the sutra repository, the consecration hall, the shrine of the护法 guardian deities, the Imperial Treasury of New Kumano, and in total, 637 temples and halls, 1,857 lay residences in Otsu, all the sutras totaling over 7,000 volumes bestowed by the Chisho, 2,000+ statues of Buddhas—all suddenly turned to smoke, which was indeed sorrowful. Even the music of the Five Delights of the various heavens must now have long ceased, and the suffering of the three fires of the dragon gods must surely have become even more intense.

Even the music of the Five Delights of the various heavens must now have long ceased, and the suffering of the three fires of the dragon gods must surely have become even more intense.

text: 夫三井寺は、近江の義大領が私の寺たりしを、天武天皇に寄奉て、御願となす。本佛も彼御門の御本尊、然るを生身の彌勒と聞え給し教待和尚百六十年行て、大師に附囑し給へり。都史多天上摩尼寶殿より天降り、遙に龍華下生の曉を待せ給ふとこそ聞つるに、こは如何にしつる事共ぞや。大師此所を傳法灌頂の靈跡として、井花水のみづをむすび給し故にこそ、三井寺とは名附たれ。かゝる目出たき聖跡なれども、今は何ならず。顯密須臾に亡て、伽藍更に跡もなし。三密道場もなければ、鈴の聲も聞えず。一夏の花も無れば、閼伽の音もせざりけり。宿老碩徳の名師は、行學に怠り、受法相承の弟子は、又經教に別んたり。寺の長吏圓慶法親王は、天王寺の別當をとゞめらる。其外僧綱十三人、闕官せられて、皆けん非違使に預らる。惡僧は筒井淨妙明秀に至るまで、三十餘人流されけり。かゝる天下の亂、國土の騒、徒事とも覺えず、平家の世末になりぬる先表やらんとぞ人申ける。

annotation.translation: As for Miidera, it was originally the temple of the imperial prince Gidai of Omi, who presented it to Emperor Tenmu as a votive offering to become his temple of prayer. The principal Buddha there is the principal image of that imperial house, yet it was heard that the Venerable Gyotai, who practiced for 160 years as the living Maitreya, received this image from the Great Master when he entrusted it to him. The Master descended from the Heavenly Jewel Hall of the Heavenly Seven Sages and awaited the dawn of the descent of the Dragon Flower from afar. Yet I have heard that this is what happened. The Great Master designated this place as the sacred site for the transmission of the esoteric consecration, and because he tied the spring water, it came to be named Miidera. Although this is such a blessed sacred site, now it is nothing but ruins. Both exoteric and esoteric teachings have perished in an instant, and the temple grounds have not even a trace left. There is no esoteric training ground, nor can one hear the sound of bells. There are no flowers of the summer retreat, nor the sound of water offerings. The renowned masters of long-standing seniority have been negligent in their practice and learning, and the disciples who received the transmission of the Dharma have turned away from the scriptures and teachings. The temple's chief official, Prince Enkyo, has been recalled to serve as the chief priest of Tennoji. Besides him, thirteen officials of the monastic hierarchy have been removed from office and are all subject to the investigation by the inspectors of misconduct. Even the evil monks, down to Tsutsui Jomyo Myoshu, have numbered over thirty and have been exiled. Unaware of this chaos in the world and the turmoil in the land, people say that the end of the Heike era has now come.
